name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 17 points on the partisan baseline
Garcia holds a massive financial edge, raising $1.2M plus $562K in outside support against roughly $600 for Fierro
Prediction markets price Garcia near 97% to win
No public general-election polling exists, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The D+17 district, Garcia's incumbency, and an overwhelming fundraising gap point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and markets agree at about 97% for Garcia. With no polls available, the margin stays near the fundamentals-based estimate rather than moving further.
model.watch: A major national political shift toward Republicans or an unforeseen candidate development could narrow the margin, though overturning a two-decade-plus deficit here would require an extraordinary swing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sylvia Garcia seeks another term in this Houston-area district, which favors Democrats by 17 points on recent partisan performance. She enters the general election with the advantages of incumbency and a dominant financial position, having raised about $1.2 million and drawn more than half a million dollars in outside support for her campaign.

Republican nominee Martha Fierro has raised only a few hundred dollars and shows no measurable campaign infrastructure in the available record. No public polls cover the race and no expert raters have ranked it, but prediction markets price Garcia's chances near 97%. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and money points to a safe Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being how large the final margin will be rather than who wins.
